risk_if_not_implemented: Without Ownership Change Provisions, supplier and External Service Provider (ESP) weaknesses, incidents or failures may propagate into the organization's environment unmanaged. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence (FOCI) (MT-17).

compensating_control_1.name: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the identification and implementation of relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual controls.
compensating_control_1.justification: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance (CPL-02) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Ownership Change Provisions (TPM-20.2) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to minimize risk associated with Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) through Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) practices.
compensating_control_2.justification: Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) (TPM-20) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Ownership Change Provisions (TPM-20.2) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
